title: powerhouse.config.json outranks environment variables; env vars are only set-if-absent build-time seeds
content:
Powerhouse services accept configuration via two methods: `.env` file (key-value pairs, loaded by `ph service start`) and `powerhouse.config.json` (structured JSON). For Connect the JSON file -- not the environment -- wins: `powerhouse.config.json` OUTRANKS env vars. When the dist config is built, values resolve lowest-to-highest as: schema defaults (`DEFAULT_CONNECT_CONFIG`) -> env-var seeds (set-if-absent; they only fill fields the source file does not specify) -> `powerhouse.config.json` at the project root, the operator's source of truth -> `ph connect build --json` -> `ph connect build --<flag>`. At runtime Connect always reads the resulting dist file as-is; it does not consult `process.env` for any field in the runtime schema. Environment variables are not a source for Connect's runtime config.

The old per-field Connect env vars are no longer wired -- PH_CONNECT_DISABLE_ADD_DRIVE, PH_CONNECT_PUBLIC_DRIVES_ENABLED, PH_CONNECT_RENOWN_URL, PH_CONNECT_RENOWN_CHAIN_ID, PH_CONNECT_LOG_LEVEL, PH_CONNECT_DEFAULT_DRIVES_URL, and the PH_CONNECT_SENTRY_* family all became `connect.*` fields in `powerhouse.config.json`. Set them by editing the file, via `ph connect config` / `ph connect build` flags, or -- for Docker -- through a single `PH_CONNECT_CONFIG_JSON` payload that the container entrypoint deep-merges into the dist file (operator-wins).

Switchboard remains genuinely env-driven: DATABASE_URL, AUTH_ENABLED, ADMINS, DEFAULT_PROTECTION. Changes require `ph service restart`.

_Corrected 2026-08-13 against Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45._
description: Connect's runtime source of truth is powerhouse.config.json. Env vars only seed fields the file omits, at build time; Connect never reads process.env at runtime.
